intent.goal: Close #386 proper: the run-close inventory's entry set is signed with the coordinator's existing Ed25519 key and run_report.py requires that signature wherever U-SIG-1's transcript rule reads the key, and provenance.retention names a concrete, offline-checkable Rekor-style receipt instead of an unspecified store — with the unsigned default path unchanged until .orca/dispatch-pubkey is committed.
intent.ruled_out: A second key scheme or any new crypto (dispatch-sign.py's canonical_record/envelope/_seed and ed25519.py are reused; inventory.py loads the signer lazily so a bundle's write/check paths never touch it); signing the raw block text instead of the entry SET (order and block membership are presentation, #315 says the claim is the union); embedding the entry list in the envelope (the record carries the entry count + the digest of the canonical set, so the envelope is one line and the same digest is what a Rekor receipt anchors); auto-discovering .orca/dispatch-pubkey from the working tree in inventory.py's CLI (it would fail the pre-key self-run reports the moment the key lands; run_report.py owns the ancestry-aware read, inventory.py takes --pubkey explicitly like verify.py's --dispatch-pubkey); dropping a stale envelope in `write` without --key (evidence is never dropped silently — it stays and check --pubkey refuses it); any change to verify.py, dispatch-sign.py or ed25519.py (out of scope — so the receipt's field-binding check is SPECIFIED in both docs and stated as not yet implemented, never claimed); any sigstore/rekor/cosign dependency or network call; raising the activation-load cap (the evidence-manifest.md clauses were paid for by compressing narrative asides in the same file, byte-neutral at 22326 vs 22330).
intent.why: The transcript closed 'a verdict the worker could not have typed'; the inventory was the remaining worker-typed input to run_report.py's binding, and the coordinator key + committed pubkey already exist as one switch. Resolving that switch once (enforcement_key) and reading it from both legs is what keeps the two rules from ever disagreeing. The receipt spec names log_index / entry_uuid / signature-over-digest because those are the fields a Rekor entry actually carries and an offline reader can bind to the signed digest; anything more (log availability, inclusion proof) needs the network and is named as not proven.
